subject: Discovery notes: embeddings + rerank — index scale, latency targets, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery notes: embeddings + rerank — index scale, latency targets, and next steps

Thanks for your time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned on pain, what you’re running today, success criteria, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Quick summary of pain points you emphasized:
- p95 response times spike during promotions; current E2E rerank adds unpredictable CPU cost and latency.
- Unit cost per customer query is trending up as index and QPS grow.
- Inconsistent relevance for long-tail queries; manual tuning of keyword fallbacks is noisy.

What we heard about your current architecture:
- Vector index: Milvus (self-hosted) backed by S3 snapshots.
- Embeddings: in-house encoder (384-d) for candidate retrieval, generated in nightly batches; occasional online upserts.
- Rerank: cross-encoder model on CPU VMs for final ordering — accurate but expensive; acts as a waterfall after dense retrieval.
- Scale: ~120M live vectors; typical traffic ~150 qps, peak ~600 qps during promos.
- Ingest pattern: nightly bulk upsert ~5M vectors; incremental stream ~100–300 vectors/sec during daytime.

Success criteria you called out:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end < 50 ms for typical retail queries (catalog retrieval + rerank).
- Relevance: measurable lift in recall@10 and NDCG on your evaluation set vs current baseline.
- Cost: reduce per-request inference/spend vs today (target: meaningful reduction in average cost, threshold TBD).
- Operational: predictable throughput with autoscaling, zero-downtime index maintenance, and SSO + SOC2 controls for procurement.

Initial POC scope (proposed):
1) Indexing: ingest a 5–10M subset from your catalog into a test index; validate vector format and shard layout.
2) Retrieval + rerank patterns: benchmark a) dense retrieval only, b) dense + lightweight cross-encoder rerank, c) hybrid (sparse + dense).
3) Latency/cost measurements: capture p50/p95 and per-request cloud GPU/CPU cost modeled at your traffic shape.
4) Success gates: p95 < 50ms OR >= 10–15% relevance lift at comparable cost.

Immediate asks from our side to scope the POC:
- Sample export (S3 link or CSV) of ~1–2M rows with id, text fields (title, description), and a small holdout of labeled queries for evaluation.
- Confirmation of your acceptable auth model (we support SSO + tokenized S3 access).
- Any non-prod security docs/policy we should know about for SOC2 review.

Next steps (proposed):
- Laura to share a one-page POC pricing and a short SOW template (attached).
- Tech deep-dive call next week with your infra lead (Tom) — options: Tue 3/24 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 3/25 14:00–15:00 PT.
- You to send sample data link and evaluation queries by EOD Tue 3/24 if possible.

Attachments: ACME_POC_scope_v1.pdf (POC scope), redwood-poc-pricing-1pager.pdf (pricing ballpark), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (security snapshot).

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

—
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-retail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery notes: embeddings + rerank — index scale, latency targets, and next steps

Thanks Jonas — helpful write-up. A few clarifying questions before we lock the POC scope: 

1) Rerank integration: currently we run dense retrieval and then a cross-encoder for final sort. For the POC, can Redwood support the same two-stage flow (retrieve 100 candidates, rerank top 100) and also measure a single-model lite rerank (e.g., distilled model) for latency comparison?

2) Index maintenance: we need to ensure nightly bulk upserts + compaction don’t cause query disruptions. How does your runtime handle background merges/flushes? Any maintenance window required?

3) Embedding compatibility: our in-house encoder is 384-d. Does the Redwood pipeline accept arbitrary dims and multiple embedding providers? We have plans to test OpenSource encoders too.

4) Security: procurement will need SOC2 and SSO options. Also whether data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys is supported for Private deployments.

Tom and I are available for the tech deep-dive on Wed 3/25 14:00 PT. If you can send a calendar invite, we’ll accept. Also please send the sample data checklist (columns/format) so we can prep the export.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Search & Personalization, Acme Retail
samira.khan@acme-retail.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-retail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery notes: embeddings + rerank — index scale, latency targets, and next steps

Looping in the pricing/SOW items as promised. Attaching: redwood-poc-pricing-1pager.pdf and ACME_POC_scope_v1.pdf.

Quick notes on the questions Samira raised:
- Two-stage flow: yes — the POC can replicate your retrieve(100)->rerank(100) pattern and we’ll capture both latency and cost for that config plus a distilled single-stage rerank.
- Index maintenance: our serving runtime uses live compaction with background merges; for Milvus-style snapshot/restore we can run without a hard maintenance window for the POC. We’ll include a tech doc in the drive link.
- Embedding dims: supported (we ingest arbitrary vector dims); you can test with your 384-d vectors or others.
- Security: we’ve added the SOC2 snapshot to the Drive link and we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments; we’ll route procurement questions to our security team if you want a full questionnaire.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed 3/25 14:00 PT and a short sample-data checklist (CSV with id, title, description, timestamp, metadata columns; one file with ~1–2M rows or staged S3 export).

—
Laura Bennett
Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Action items we’ve committed to:

- Jonas: prepare a short test plan and runbook for the POC; will include baseline queries, evaluation metrics (recall@10, NDCG), and ingestion checklist.

- Security: Laura to surface SOC2 snapshot and options for CMK in the Drive folder.

If anything changes on your side, reply-all and we’ll re-align. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
